title: Detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction with a gate-tunable van der Waals tunneling photodetector
task: Incorporate gate-tunable photodetector response in cross-spectral image prediction
key_results: Achieved PSNR 26.58 dB and SSIM 0.89 in visible-to-infrared prediction; reduced detector-space error relative to controls; post-inference measurements confirmed 64-mask response consistency
comments: Detector-response layer as differentiable constraint is conceptually novel but validation limited to specific van der Waals device; generalization to other detector types unclear.

model_io.model: Cross-spectral prediction network with differentiable detector-response layer
inputs: gate-tunable PdSe2/h-BN/WSe2 detector response manifold (wavelength, power, bias, gate voltage)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Detector response manifold constrains prediction consistency while preserving image fidelity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: framework reduces detector-space error; post-inference measurements validate response consistency

title: Exciton-driven Floquet engineering from first principles
task: First-principles prediction of Floquet engineering driven by exciton dynamics
key_results: Captured subgap excitonic resonance in monolayer h-BN; demonstrated oscillatory excitonic field generates Floquet sidebands and band renormalization without temporal pump-probe overlap
comments: Computationally efficient framework combining real-time TDDFT with modified kernel is promising but validation limited to h-BN; applicability to other materials and higher excitation densities needs exploration.

model_io.model: First-principles Floquet framework (real-time TDDFT + modified long-range-corrected kernel + Floquet-band analysis)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Exciton-driven oscillatory field generates Floquet engineering without direct laser dressing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: clear Floquet sidebands observed in h-BN even without pump-probe temporal overlap

title: Cometary impacts an unlikely pathway towards the origins of life on Earth
task: Reassess role of cometary bombardment in delivering prebiotic molecules for life's origins on Earth
key_results: Rapid decline in cometary impact bombardment; significant proportion of volatile organics destroyed during hypervelocity impact; successful delivery of prebiotic feedstock molecules identified as exceedingly rare event
comments: Challenges long-held assumption through rigorous modeling but does not rule out cometary contribution entirely; complementary abiotic synthesis pathways on early Earth may dominate prebiotic chemistry.

model_io.model: Cometary impact simulation + comet-atmosphere interaction + dynamical modeling of short-period comet evolution

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cometary impacts deliver significant prebiotic feedstock in high concentrations required for prebiotic chemistry
hypotheses.result: Refuted: organic destruction during impact and declining bombardment rate make this pathway exceedingly rare

title: Machine learning for advancing gamma source localization in a human phantom using NaI (Tl) detector spectra in radiobioassay
task: Localize gamma radiation sources in human phantom using machine learning on detector spectra
key_results: Logistic regression achieved 100% localization accuracy for GI organ (thyroid excluded); decision tree up to 97.4%; performance degraded for Ba-133 and whole-body detector due to spectral overlap and symmetry
comments: Feature-based modular approach is practical for constrained settings but struggles with low-energy isotopes and symmetric geometries; limited training data constrains SVM/MLP applicability.

model_io.model: Modular ML classification pipeline (LR, DT, SVM, MLP per isotope-detector pair)
inputs: NaI(Tl) energy spectra from Co-60, Cs-137, Ba-133
ten statistical features (mean, skewness, kurtosis, entropy, IQR, etc.)
outputs: organ localization predictions (GI, lung, thyroid, WB)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Logistic regression and decision tree outperform SVM/MLP for source localization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: LR/DT achieved >97% accuracy; SVM/MLP performance poor due to limited data and feature sensitivity

title: Hierarchical structure of primary and hybridization-induced superconducting correlations in bilayer nickelates
task: Explain microscopic pairing mechanism in bilayer nickelate superconductors
key_results: Primary pairing originates from bonding-antibonding splitting of Ni 3dz² orbitals; orbital hybridization redistributes correlations to dx²-y² channel, explaining comparable long-range correlations in both channels
comments: Variational Monte Carlo on simplified two-orbital model provides insight but direct experimental verification of orbital-specific pairing channels remains challenging.

outputs: pairing correlations in each orbital channel

hypotheses.hypothesis: Orbital hybridization redistributes superconducting correlations despite weak intrinsic pairing tendency in dx²-y²
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: comparable long-range correlations observed in both channels

title: A nanoscale map of the human cell surface proteome reveals spatial and functional organization
task: Map spatial organization and functional modules of human cell surface proteome
key_results: Identified 85 surface antigens organized into functional modules including TCR complexes and novel membrane-associated mitochondrial proteins; ML classifier revealed IL-10Rβ regulation of type I interferon signaling
comments: Novel discovery of mitochondrial proteins at plasma membrane warrants functional validation beyond proximity labeling artifacts.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cell surface proteins are organized into functional spatial modules
hypotheses.result: Identified known complexes (TCR) and novel clusters; spatial modeling distinguishes dispersed vs. localized antigens

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mitochondrial proteins localize to plasma membrane with functional roles
hypotheses.result: Detected mitochondrial proteins at cell surface; roles remain to be characterized

hypotheses.hypothesis: IL-10Rβ regulates type I interferon signaling
hypotheses.result: ML classifier predicted this regulatory relationship from association data
